messages:
Alex: Heads-up from today's usability pass on the model catalog compare table. A few small-but-visible UX regressions I want to flag.
Alex: 1) The performance legend is buried in the help menu. folks missed it and assumed badges were arbitrary.
Alex: 2) When switching list density the compare column widths jump and reflow, which hides the pinned indicator momentarily.
Mei: Re: legend: agree — we should make a compact legend available in the table header (help icon) and also expose a concise label on hover/focus for each badge.
Mei: For copy, propose: "Latency-first — P95 under 50ms (reference)" and "Balanced — P95 50150ms" and "Throughput-first — optimized for rps". Short and scannable.
Carlos: About the reflow: the repro is when density toggle animates heights. Browser paints push the compare column and the pin icon gets clipped for a frame. Might be a flexbox vs absolute positioned icon issue.
Carlos: Quick fix suggestion: make pin icon absolutely positioned relative to row container so it doesn't move with text reflow.
Alex: Nice. Also, some users interpreted the green "fast" badge as "cheaper". So tooltip needs explicit axis label: latency vs cost vs throughput.
Mei: Tooltip idea: title = "Performance: Latency-first" body = "Measured as P95 latency on reference harness (50ms). Not a cost metric." Add link "Learn how we measure" that opens a tiny modal.
UXResearcher: From research: 42% of participants expected badge to include unit info. The modal would reduce follow-ups. Recommend tracking clicks on the modal link as an event.
Alex: Agree. Add analytics: `catalog.performance.legend.open` with props { tier: string }.
Mei: Accessibility: ensure badge has aria-describedby pointing to the tooltip content ID when visible, and aria-label that reads fully when focused. Also avoid relying on color alone; include a small shape difference (dot, dash) for each tier.
a11y-bot: Checklist: 1) Badge must have aria-label describing tier and axis (e.g., "Performance: latency-first, P95 < 50ms"). 2) Tooltip/modal must be keyboard operable and trap focus. 3) Density toggle should preserve keyboard focus and not hide active indicators. 4) Color+shape combos for non-color vision users.
Carlos: Implementation snippet for pin position:

```
.row {
  position: relative;
}
.pin-icon {
  position: absolute;
  right: 12px;
  top: 50%;
  transform: translateY(-50%);
}
```

Mei: For the compact legend in header: small help icon with aria-haspopup that opens the modal. On small viewports collapse the help into the overflow menu.
Alex: One more microcopy nit: current filter pill says "fuzzy" which is internal shorthand. Change to "Fuzzy match" and show a short hint: "matches model names and descriptions" on hover.
UXResearcher: Will add that to the copy doc and include user-friendly examples.
Mei: Next steps: I'll mock the header legend + tooltip copy and include shape variants. Carlos will patch pin positioning and density animation in a small PR. Alex to file analytics event.
Alex: Plan to ship as non-flagged patch; schedule a quick smoke test on staging once PRs are in.
Carlos: I'll run cross-browser check for the absolute pin fix.
Mei: Dropping Figma link (WIP): https://www.figma.com/file/NEW/compare-legend-microcopy
Alex: Thanks all. If anyone else spots similar surprises during review, drop screenshots here. :wave:
